<!-- pr-reviewer: 0722074d6b7a55a5391110c4fe7d2c7debf9ab49 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Full-rigour review (collision judgement, safety floor), trial-merged with `upstream/main` (clean, no conflicts), built on macOS with its own target.

**What looks good**
- Every work-turning rotary now gets one of four outcomes in `rotary_line` / `verdict` (posting_index_swing.rs:70-130): `Horizontal(u)` is judged, `Vertical` is safe, and `Leaning` (including zero or non-finite vectors) and `Unknown` are refused by name. There is no path where an unclassified rotary reads as clear.
- Tilted line: a stated vector must be within 1e-6 of level or vertical, otherwise it is refused as "neither level nor vertical". It is never judged "approximately level".
- The math holds. A vertical tool tip at height h is at least h from any level line through the origin, so `nose_to_axis - tool length >= swept + 5 mm` is conservative for any level u. The sweep is the full circle regardless of index angle or G30 position.
- Machine without an envelope: an unstated or non-finite `nose_to_axis` refuses by name for B as for A (:171-190). A non-finite facet vertex now means an unbounded sweep, so the post is refused (previously skipped).
- Two work-turning rotaries: the sweep is taken from the WCS origin (every line passes through it, and tip distance from the origin is also >= h), so a stacked table is not judged about a single line. Conservative.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`/casts added; layering and provenance fine; decision record present; no snapshot, golden or CHANGELOG edits; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #818`. Process files untouched, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is needed. Files are under 400 lines.
- Shipped machines are unchanged (only the microARC A turns the work on a level line).

**Local results (merged with main)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `index_swing_horizontal` (new) | 10 passed |
| `index_swing` | 9 passed |
| `tormach_fourth_axis` | 12 passed |
| `rotary_letter` / `rotary_verify` | 3 / 9 passed |
| `posting` / `machine` / `conformance` / `microarc_test_part` | 17 / 33 / 6 / 2 passed |
| `camcraft-app --lib` / `project_roundtrip` / `setup_wcs` | 110 / 71 / 7 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the full 62-suite app step of the quick plan, only the swing, rotary, posting, machine and project suites above. No existing post golden changed (none touched by the diff).

**Pinning coverage by axis kind**: A about X (existing `index_swing`: hits and clears), B (hit `a_table_b_too_long...`, clear `a_table_b_with_a_short_tool_clears`), A stated level but off X (hit and clear in one test), unstated-vector B, C (stays unjudged), leaning/zero/non-finite (refused), B+C stacked (origin sweep).

**Interaction with #951 / #952 (and #950)**: `git merge-tree` of this head against #951 (83cf9c6b) and #952 (ce987857) is clean for each. Those PRs touch only `assets/posts/*.cps`, `crates/post/src/post/*`, and their own tests; this PR touches none of them, and the index-swing gate is upstream of the post. Merge order does not matter; no re-check needed after either.

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. A machine file can only state the rotary's direction (`axis`), not an offset, so "offset axis line" is covered only through the existing law that the WCS origin lies on the rotary's line. A shipped table with an offset line cannot be expressed; worth a follow-up issue if one is ever needed.
2. A leaning or unknown work-turning rotary refuses every op on that machine, even a 3-axis program that never indexes. Consistent with #813, and the message tells the user what to fix in the machine file.
3. The PR says no posted table-B program that clears was exercised; the gate-only test is accepted.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 0722074d6b7a55a5391110c4fe7d2c7debf9ab49 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is an independent review, done at the high tier because the change touches a collision check at the post gate. The earlier marker review on this head was posted by the author's own account.

**What looks good**
- The geometry holds for any level line. A vertical tool at height h above a horizontal line through the origin is at least h from that line, so the tip is the tool's nearest point to it. The sweep `|(p - o) x u|` (`posting_index_swing.rs:172-181`) reduces to main's `hypot(y, z)` when u is X, so A-about-X verdicts are the same algebraically.
- The sweep covers a full revolution, so the sign of the axis vector, the rotary-direction field (#803) and the travel limits cannot make a real swing pass. I checked that an inverted `[0,-1,0]` B and an inverted `[-1,0,0]` A give the same verdicts as their standard versions.
- Nothing falls through to "judged clean". A leaning line, a zero vector or a non-finite vector refuses by name, and so does an unknown letter with no vector or an unstated `nose_to_axis` on any level rotary. With two work-turning rotaries, any one leaning or nose-less rotary refuses. The `level > 0.0` / `len > 0.0` guards rule out dividing by a zero vector.
- With stacked rotaries the sweep is taken from the WCS origin (`:280`), which is conservative.
- The load note now names a table B (`project/swing_note.rs:34`).
- No unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. Both files are under 400 lines. The tests live in `camcraft-app`, which owns the behaviour. The decision file is complete.
- The new refusal message is plain English and tells the user what to change ("state a level or vertical "axis" for B in the machine file").
- No MCP or command side is needed, because this is a gate and adds no user command.

**Local results (Windows, trial-merged with main a6bd69d8, merge clean)**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| index_swing_horizontal (new) | 10 passed |
| index_swing | 9 passed |
| fourth_axis_pose | 9 passed |
| tormach_fourth_axis | 12 passed |
| machine | 33 passed |
| tilt | 8 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| golden_cl | 25 passed (goldens untouched) |
| app lib `swing` | 1 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Reviewer's own scratch tests** (not committed). All four passed against the PR:
- **Axis tell-apart.** A bar 1.5 in long along X, with the tip 30 mm above the line. A table B refuses it (sweep 39.27 mm). The A-about-X machine clears the same setup.
- **Bar along the B line.** A bar along Y clears on B.
- **Offset and mirror.** A 10 mm block 100-110 mm out along +X, and its mirror at -X, both sweep 110.11 mm on B and are refused; on A both clear. A part 60 mm tall, above or below the line, is refused on both B and A.
- **Refusals.** `[0,1,0.01]`, `[1,0,-0.2]`, `[0.7,0,0.7]` and `[0,1,1e-5]` are all refused by name. A B with no `nose_to_axis` is refused, and so are an A and a lettered B with neither a vector nor a nose. A rotary `U` with no vector, B plus a leaning C, and B plus an A with no nose are each refused by name.

**Shipped machines.** The only shipped machines with a work-turning rotary are the microARC (A `[1,0,0]`, nose stated) and the Doosan DNM (A `[1,0,0]`, no nose, refused on main as well). Neither verdict changes. The A and B on tilthead and the C on millturn carry the head, so they are still not judged.

**A-about-X differences from main** (none on a shipped machine; each one is stricter or more correct):
1. A non-finite vertex now refuses; main skipped it.
2. A stated vector that leans up to about 5.7 degrees off X was judged about X on main; it is now refused as leaning.
3. An A that has a second work-turning rotary now sweeps from the origin.
4. A level A stated off X is now judged about its own line instead of about X.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (non-blocking)**
1. The rotary line is assumed to pass through the WCS origin, as main assumes for A. The machine file has no field for the axis position, and nothing checks that the setup's WCS sits on the B line. For a table B, the user would have to put X0 Z0 on the B centerline. This assumption predates this PR; a follow-up issue could either check it or state it on the setup sheet.
2. `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (around lines 109-123) still describes the clause as "a work-turning A about X". It could name any level line and the leaning refusal.
3. In the stacked case the message mixes letters, e.g. "turns the work on A but states no nose_to_axis ... swept by the B0.000 index". `letter` is the first level rotary and `r` is the nose-less one. This is cosmetic.
4. The index angle in the message is read from the stated vector's sign, not from the rotary-direction field (#803). It is only display text, so it does not affect the verdict.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
